job.title: HR Business Partner
job.description:

The Opportunity

As a Human Resources Business Partner, you will act as a trusted advisor to senior leaders, developing and delivering commercially aligned people strategies that support business objectives.

Working within a collaborative HR function, you will have the opportunity to influence organisational change, uplift leadership capability and contribute to a high-performing culture.

Key responsibilities include:

  • Build trusted relationships with senior leaders, providing strategic and commercially focused HR advice.
  • Partner with stakeholders to develop and execute people plans aligned to business objectives.
  • Provide guidance on complex employee relations, performance management and workplace matters.
  • Support organisational design, restructures and change management initiatives.
  • Coach and influence leaders to strengthen people management capability and drive accountability.
  • Leverage people insights, workforce metrics and remuneration benchmarking to inform decision-making.
  • Collaborate with specialist HR teams to deliver effective and consistent people solutions.
  • Mentor and support HR colleagues, contributing to a collaborative and high-performing function.


About You

We are seeking an experienced HR professional who brings a strong combination of commercial acumen, strategic thinking and hands-on business partnering capability.
You will be confident engaging with senior stakeholders, comfortable navigating complex people matters and passionate about delivering practical solutions that make a genuine difference.

To be successful, you will bring:

  • Demonstrated experience in a Human Resources Business Partner role within a complex organisation.
  • Strong stakeholder engagement skills, with the confidence to influence and challenge senior leaders.
  • Broad generalist HR experience, particularly across employee relations, organisational development and change management.
  • A commercial mindset and the ability to align people strategies with broader business priorities.
  • Experience supporting organisational change and leadership capability development.
  • Strong coaching, problem-solving and relationship-building skills.
  • The ability to balance competing priorities in a fast-paced environment.


Why Consider This Opportunity?

This is a fantastic opportunity to join an established HR function where you can genuinely influence business outcomes through strategic partnering.

You will work alongside experienced HR professionals, build strong relationships with senior leaders and play a key role in delivering people initiatives that support continued business success.

If you are looking for an opportunity to combine strategic influence, commercial partnering and hands-on HR expertise, we would love to hear from you.

job.title: Senior Commercial Merchandise Manager
job.description:
Blue Bungalow has built a successful business by knowing their customer, choosing product she loves and being prepared to move quickly when they see an opportunity.

They’re an established Australian fashion and lifestyle brand with a loyal customer following and ambitious plans for continued growth. While the business has grown, they’ve remained entrepreneurial, hands-on and close to their customer. They also want to keep it that way.

We’re looking for a Senior Commercial Merchandise Manager to lead their buying team and take ownership of the commercial performance of the merchandise function. Working closely with the Founder, Creative Merchandise Manager and Financial Controller, you’ll bring a strong commercial view to the way they buy. You’ll help determine where they invest, how much they invest and when they need to change course, while leading a team that knows their product and customer incredibly well.

The role
Leading the buying team, the Senior Commercial Merchandise Manager will set clear direction around investment, inventory and performance, with ownership of open-to-buy, merchandise budgets, cash flow and inventory health.

This means staying close to sales and stock performance, understanding where there is an opportunity to invest more and recognising when it’s time to pull back. With product sourced through wholesale, production orders and our own direct development, there is also an important balance to strike between margin opportunity, inventory and cash.

The role works closely with the Creative Merchandise Manager, bringing commercial insight to product decisions while recognising the importance of customer knowledge and creative instinct. It is also an important link into Finance, providing a clear and trusted view of merchandise performance and investment.

Just as importantly, this person will lead and develop the buying team, creating clear accountability and building strong commercial capability across the function.

About you
Your background is likely to be in merchandise planning, merchandise management or commercial buying within fashion, retail or apparel.

Strong capability across open-to-buy, inventory investment, forecasting, margin, stock turn and cash is important, alongside the judgement to know what the numbers mean and what action to take.

You’ll be a confident leader, comfortable setting direction, challenging thinking and making decisions, while giving experienced people the space to do their jobs well.

Blue Bungalow is founder-led, fast-moving and collaborative. We’re looking for someone who enjoys that environment, can operate comfortably at both a strategic and hands-on level, and understands the balance between commercial discipline and great retail instinct.

Why Blue Bungalow?
This is an opportunity to have genuine influence in a successful Australian business as it enters its next stage of growth.

They want to strengthen the commercial capability behind their merchandise decisions while retaining the pace, creativity and understanding of their customer that have made Blue Bungalow what it is today.

job.title: General Manager People Experience
job.description:

The role will bring these areas together to deliver consistent, practical and contemporary support for leaders and employees.

This role has the scope to shape the People Experience function by strengthening its structure, capability, processes and ways of working. The focus is practical: enabling so leaders and employees to perform at their best and supported to deliver Dementia Australia’s purpose the organisation’s purpose.

Your experience may come from a commercial, corporate, service-based or similarly complex environment. Sector experience is less important than your ability to lead a high-performing People function, bring fresh thinking and translate contemporary practice into outcomes that work in Dementia Australia’s context.

You will bring broad People leadership experience, strong business partnering capability and a track record of leading geographically dispersed teams through change and improvement. You will be confident addressing capability and performance, constructively challenging established ways of working, and translating strategic priorities into pragmatic delivery.

Importantly, you will be someone who can imagine what could be next - a leader who sees opportunities, creates solutions and brings people with them.

Why Dementia Australia?
This is an opportunity to bring your commercial People experience into an organisation where the work has genuine meaning.

Dementia Australia offers the opportunity to work nationally, influence senior leaders and shape a People Experience function with meaningful scope for improvement. Based in Milton, Brisbane, the role offers a hybrid working environment, with an expectation that this senior leader will also value the importance of visible leadership, connection and collaboration in the office and through some national travel.

For a People leader who wants the scope to shape, create and influence – while contributing to an organisation with genuine purpose – this is a compelling next move.

job.title: Executive General Manager - Field and Asset Management
job.description:
Powerlink Queensland is at the centre of Queensland’s energy future, operating the high-voltage transmission network that connects Queenslanders to a safe, reliable and affordable energy system.

An opportunity now exists to join Powerlink’s Executive Team as Executive General Manager, Field & Asset Management, leading one of the organisation’s largest and most operationally critical divisions.

Reporting to the Chief Executive, the role is responsible for the safe, reliable and efficient operation and management of Powerlink’s transmission network. The portfolio brings together asset management, operational engineering, field delivery and operational support services, with approximately 530 people working across a geographically dispersed, 24/7 environment.

This is a broad executive role spanning asset strategy, field delivery and maintenance. A key focus will be ensuring an integrated approach to managing Powerlink’s extensive linear infrastructure, connecting centralised asset management and planning with effective execution in the field. You will balance safety, reliability, asset performance and cost, while ensuring maintenance and operational programs are appropriately prioritised and resourced.

As a member of the Executive Team, you will contribute beyond the portfolio, working closely with the Chief Executive and executive colleagues to shape organisational priorities and Powerlink’s broader strategic direction. Leading a large and diverse workforce, you will build capability, foster strong leadership and continue to evolve ways of working across operational and field environments.

We are seeking an accomplished executive with experience leading large-scale linear infrastructure, ideally within electricity transmission or distribution, telecommunications or a comparable network environment. You will bring a strong understanding of centralised asset management and strategy, coupled with the realities of maintenance and field delivery across a geographically dispersed network.

A visible and credible leader, you will set a strong tone for safety, leadership and performance, building trusted relationships across the workforce and creating an environment where people are engaged, supported and clear on the contribution they make. Your ability to lead through influence, navigate complexity and bring people with you will be critical.

Commercially astute, you will balance operational performance and reliability with longer-term asset investment, ensuring decisions support the safe, efficient and sustainable performance of the network.

This is a significant opportunity to lead a critical part of Powerlink’s business and contribute to the delivery of Queensland’s Energy Roadmap at a pivotal time for the sector.

job.title: Executive Director – Enterprise Transformation
job.description:
Lutheran Services is a respected, values-driven organisation delivering aged care, retirement living and community services across Queensland. With a proud history of supporting individuals and communities, the organisation is entering an exciting period of growth and transformation, focused on strengthening service delivery, innovation and long-term sustainability.

Reporting to the Chief Executive Officer and as a key member of the Executive Leadership Team, the Executive Director – Enterprise Transformation will lead a diverse portfolio of strategic initiatives spanning digital and technology, organisational change, major capital development, operational improvement and mergers and acquisitions. This is a pivotal role in translating strategy into action, strengthening enterprise-wide governance and ensuring complex transformation programs deliver meaningful and sustainable outcomes.

Working collaboratively across the organisation, you will lead the enterprise project management and change functions, oversee significant capital and infrastructure investments, and support strategic growth opportunities. The portfolio includes major property developments, business improvement initiatives and potential acquisitions, requiring sound commercial judgement, disciplined execution and a strong understanding of organisational priorities. Success will require the ability to balance commercial discipline and delivery excellence with genuine engagement, ensuring change is embraced and embedded across the organisation.

Beyond the delivery of individual programs, you will play an important role in building organisational capability and creating a consistent, enterprise-wide approach to transformation. Central to your success will be the ability to bring people with you, build trust across diverse stakeholder groups and foster a culture of shared ownership and accountability. You will understand that sustainable transformation is achieved through people, not simply processes, and that the way change is led is just as important as the outcomes delivered.

You will be an accomplished executive with demonstrated experience leading complex transformation portfolios in large, service-oriented organisations. Commercially astute and strategically minded, you will bring strong governance, program delivery and change leadership capability, alongside experience in capital development and mergers and acquisitions. Equally important will be your leadership philosophy and alignment with Lutheran Services' values. You will be a genuine servant leader who leads with humility, integrity and empathy, placing people and purpose at the centre of your decisions. Approachable, collaborative and grounded, you will be comfortable challenging thinking while listening openly, empowering others and building strong, trusting relationships. Experience in aged care, health, community services or the not-for-profit sector will be highly regarded, however cultural alignment and a genuine commitment to the organisation's mission will be paramount.

This is an opportunity to make a lasting contribution to a highly regarded organisation, shaping its future while supporting the delivery of meaningful services to Queensland communities.

For more information, please contact Gemma Ledbury on 0423 322 462

job.title: Head of People and Culture
job.description:
The Opportunity
An exciting opportunity exists for an experienced and commercially minded Head of People & Culture to join a successful, founder-led Australian business entering its next phase of growth and transformation.

Entrepreneurial, fast-moving and customer-focused, this business has built a strong reputation and an engaged workforce. With ambitious plans ahead, the focus is now on building the people capability, leadership frameworks and organisational foundations to support sustainable growth.

Reporting directly to the Founder and Managing Director, you will have the opportunity to build and shape the People & Culture function, bringing structure, contemporary HR practices and a clear people strategy to a business that values creativity, agility and performance.

This is a role for someone who enjoys building rather than maintaining, can move comfortably between strategy and execution, and thrives in an environment where they can make a visible impact.

Your Focus

  • Build the function: Establish the People & Culture strategy, frameworks, processes and operating rhythms to support a growing business.
  • Partner with the Founder: Act as a trusted advisor, translating business ambition into practical people priorities and outcomes.
  • Develop leadership capability: Coach and empower leaders, build accountability and introduce contemporary performance and development frameworks.
  • Shape culture and engagement: Protect what makes the business special while evolving a high-performance, high-care culture.
  • Enable growth and change: Support organisational design, workforce planning, succession and change initiatives as the business scales.
  • Elevate the employee experience: Strengthen talent acquisition, onboarding, retention, recognition and career development.
  • Establish operational excellence: Build fit-for-purpose HR policies, systems and processes, ensuring strong governance and employment compliance.


About You
You will be an accomplished HR or People & Culture leader who brings the confidence, energy and commercial judgement to establish a function and influence at all levels of a business.

Ideally, your experience will have been gained in customer-centric organisations with diverse operational workforces, where you understand the balance between commercial performance, employee experience and operational delivery.

You will bring:

  • Broad HR leadership experience, with demonstrated success building or transforming people functions.
  • Experience supporting growing, entrepreneurial or founder-led organisations, where agility and adaptability are essential.
  • Strong organisational development, leadership capability and change management expertise.
  • A sound understanding of Australian employment legislation, employee relations and contemporary HR practices.
  • The ability to engage and influence across leadership, corporate and frontline operational teams.
  • A pragmatic, hands-on style, balanced with the strategic thinking and commercial acumen to support business growth.

Importantly, you will be someone who brings ideas, creates momentum and knows how to turn strategy into action. You are comfortable challenging constructively, building trusted relationships and introducing structure without losing the entrepreneurial spirit that has made a business successful.

Why Consider This Opportunity?
This is a rare opportunity to take ownership of the people agenda within an ambitious, founder-led business, with the autonomy to build something meaningful.

You will work closely with an engaged Founder, influence business direction and play a pivotal role in shaping the culture, capability and organisational foundations for the next chapter.

Based on Brisbane's CBD fringes, with onsite parking available.

job.title: ER Specialist
job.description:
About the organisation
Our client is a large, well-established and purpose-driven organisation with a diverse workforce and a strong commitment to delivering meaningful outcomes for the communities it serves.

With a complex operational environment and a focus on continuous improvement, the organisation is seeking an experienced ER Specialist to join its broader People & Culture function.

This is an exciting opportunity to join a team focused on strengthening its employee relations capability, building trusted relationships across the business and creating a more proactive and collaborative approach to managing workplace matters.

About the role
Reporting to the Employee Relations Manager, the ER Specialist will play a key role in providing specialist advice and support to leaders across the organisation.

Working closely with HR Business Partners and operational stakeholders, you will manage a broad range of employee relations matters, providing practical, commercially considered advice while building leadership capability and supporting positive workplace outcomes.

Key responsibilities will include:

  • Managing complex employee relations matters, including performance management, grievances, disciplinary matters, complaints and ill or injured worker cases.
  • Conducting and supporting workplace investigations, ensuring fair, consistent and timely outcomes.
  • Providing specialist advice on employment legislation, awards, enterprise agreements and organisational policies.
  • Coaching and supporting leaders to confidently navigate challenging employee matters.
  • Building strong, trusted relationships with stakeholders across a diverse and complex operational environment.
  • Supporting the development and delivery of employee relations training, policies and continuous improvement initiatives.
  • Contributing to broader HR projects and initiatives to strengthen the effectiveness of the ER function.

About you
You will be an experienced ER Specialist who brings strong technical expertise, sound judgement and a genuine passion for partnering with leaders to achieve positive outcomes.

You will be comfortable navigating complex and sensitive matters, balancing legislative requirements with practical solutions and building credibility with stakeholders at all levels.

To be successful, you will bring:

  • Demonstrated experience managing a broad range of complex employee relations matters and workplace investigations.
  • Strong working knowledge of employment legislation, industrial instruments and ER frameworks.
  • Excellent stakeholder engagement, influencing and coaching capability.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving and decision-making skills.
  • The ability to manage competing priorities and sensitive matters with professionalism and discretion.
  • Relevant tertiary qualifications in Human Resources or a related discipline, or equivalent practical experience.

What's on offer?
This is a fantastic opportunity to join a purpose-driven organisation where you can make a genuine impact on the employee experience and the way employee relations is delivered across the business.

You will work alongside experienced HR professionals, contribute to the ongoing development of the ER function and have the opportunity to build meaningful relationships with leaders across a diverse workforce.

If you are an experienced ER Specialist looking for your next challenge in a collaborative and evolving environment, we would love to hear from you.

job.title: Community Engagement & Partnerships Manager
job.description:
Mackay Women’s Services is seeking an experienced and purpose-driven Community Engagement and Partnerships Manager to lead community connection, strategic partnerships, marketing and growth initiatives that strengthen their impact across the Mackay region.

This is a unique opportunity to join an organisation delivering critical frontline services and create meaningful change through building relationships, raising awareness and driving sustainable community outcomes.

About the Organisation

Mackay Women’s Services is a respected not-for-profit organisation supporting women, children and communities affected by domestic and family violence and sexual assault across the Mackay, Isaac and Whitsunday regions.

Their work spans counselling, crisis response, safety planning, education, community awareness and behaviour change programs, all underpinned by a commitment to being Holistic, Ethical, Respectful and Socially Just.

About the Opportunity

Reporting into the CEO, this role will lead the organisation’s community engagement and partnership strategy while enhancing visibility, strengthening stakeholder relationships and creating opportunities for long-term sustainability.

You will work across community, government, corporate and funding networks to increase awareness, deepen community connection and diversify support for their services.

Key responsibilities include:

  • Develop and deliver community engagement and partnership initiatives aligned to organisational strategy
  • Build and maintain strong relationships with community stakeholders, government, sponsors and local businesses
  • Identify and grow partnership, sponsorship and funding opportunities
  • Coordinate grants and support submissions to diversify income streams
  • Lead marketing and communication campaigns across digital and traditional channels
  • Manage social media, website content and public communications
  • Plan and deliver events, workshops and outreach activities
  • Create compelling content including newsletters, campaigns, media releases and impact stories
  • Monitor engagement outcomes and provide insights to support continuous improvement
  • Coordinate volunteer engagement and strengthen community participation


About You
You are a relationship builder who combines strategic thinking with a hands-on approach and are passionate about creating positive social impact.

You will bring:

  • Experience in community engagement, partnerships, business development, marketing or fundraising
  • Strong stakeholder management and networking capability
  • Experience developing initiatives that build community awareness and engagement
  • Exposure to grants, sponsorships or funding opportunities
  • Excellent written communication and content development skills
  • Confidence managing multiple projects and competing priorities
  • Experience across digital platforms and communications channels
  • Qualifications in Marketing, Communications, Public Relations or a related discipline (preferred)


Why Join?

  • Make a genuine impact in the lives of women and families in the Mackay region
  • Join a values-led organisation committed to community outcomes
  • Shape and grow a newly broadened role with influence across the organisation
  • Work within a supportive and purpose-driven team environment


If you are excited by the opportunity to connect communities, create partnerships and drive meaningful outcomes, we’d love to hear from you.
